title: Gifts For Game Masters, Players, And The Whole Table - 2026 Edition
summary: Be you a Dungeons & Dragons party, Daggerheart devotee, or Mothership truther, we've got ideas to spark your imagination.
body_markdown:
The time for gift-giving is upon us once again. Perhaps your game group is engaging in a Secret Santa or White Elephant. Or maybe your partner is the Game Master who owns every rulebook in existence. Whatever the case, we've summoned up a comprehensive gift guide for every person at the table. Be you a Dungeons & Dragons party, *Daggerheart* devotee, or[Mothership](https://startplaying.games/play/mothership) truther, we've got ideas to spark your imagination.


## **For Game Masters**


### **REMONSTERED! The Monsters Know What They're Doing: Updated Combat Tactics For Up-To-Date Dungeon Masters**


via Simon & Schuster


If you know someone well into their first DnD campaign or looking to become a pro Dungeon Master, this is the[book to gift them](https://startplaying.games/blog/posts/remonstered-monsters-know-what-theyre-doing-review-dnd-book) . Assuming, of course, that they’re running the latest DnD rules from the *2024 Player’s Handbook* also called 5.5e.[REMONSTERED](https://www.thriftbooks.com/w/untitled-mk-the-monsters-know-what-theyre-doing_keith-ammann/58357646/item/88412801/?isbn=1668236931&idiq=88412801&utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=shopping_new_condition_books_high_14637440387&utm_adgroup=&utm_term=&utm_content=593819619485&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=14637440387&gbraid=0AAAAADwY45jqsTne6XtMvg0PIVYkSXscb&gclid=EAIaIQobChMInrLsrIGOmAMVTSFECB2TeCAOEAQYASABEgKUU_D_BwE) ** acts as a guide to leveling up their combats by making the most of monster abilities. It’s especially great for DMs who get really into the roleplay aspect of the game but need help with tactics.


### **The Map Library**


via Roll & Play Press


This here is one of the best gifts I’ve ever gotten from my players. The maps are vibrant and depict pretty much every common fantasy location a party could find themselves in.[The Map Library](https://rollandplaypress.com/products/the-map-library?tw_source=google&tw_adid=&tw_campaign=23714187065&tw_kwdid=&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23718833422&gbraid=0AAAAAqQyLfDwS9iBJw_lnfeFPe0txHWJq&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI-vOU-oOOmAMVuZHuAR2qQgo-EAAYASAAEgKo8fD_BwE) is a perfect blend of detailed enough to grab players’ attentions and generic enough to be endlessly reusable. The maps are also organized very well, always being easy to find at a moment’s notice. Finally, the box itself is a sturdy container so you can take all 100 maps with you on the go.


### **Terrain Set Or Digital Asset Pack**


via HRC Wargaming


Should the party all want to chip in for a big GM gift, a nice set of tabletop terrain is always appreciated. It can feel personal, too, if you get something resembling your party’s home base or ship. Etsy[has a lot of options](https://www.etsy.com/c/toys-and-games/toys/miniature-toys/role-playing-miniatures?gpla=1&gao=1&utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=shopping_us_ps-c-toys_and_games&utm_custom1=_k_EAIaIQobChMI0crX95aQmAMVXCNECB1ORxZSEAQYASABEgK2kvD_BwE_k_&utm_content=go_21791666334_169566861518_716586688971_pla-314535279060_c__4396350708_12768591&utm_custom2=21791666334&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21791666334&gbraid=0AAAAADtcfRK7eDVARwTMXxXUKu6nyWJzF&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI0crX95aQmAMVXCNECB1ORxZSEAQYASABEgK2kvD_BwE&explicit=1&ref=catnav_breadcrumb-3) with varying price points that can fit most TTRPG settings. The popular options tend to feature fantasy towns, castles, and sci-fi cities. Though you can also find more broad-use options like hills, tree packs, and technology pieces.


If your GM tends to run their games online, this gift can still work in the form of asset packs. These are basically a big folder with pictures of buildings, spaceships, dungeon set dressing, characters of different time periods, and so much more. These can be purchased through the Roll20 store, Foundry Marketplace, or generic stores like[DriveThruRPG](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/browse?keyword=token) .


### **A Game With A StartPlaying GM**


Seriously, it’s not just an advertisement; we GMs want to play too. For me in particular, there are several new games I want to try but my friends will never run. But I know there’s plenty of StartPlaying Game Masters running[Lancer one-shots](https://startplaying.games/play/lancer) – I’ve been keeping my eye on them. So get your GM a[StartPlaying gift card](https://startplaying.games/gift-card) so they can finally play *Lancer* – I mean their white whale game.


### **WizKids Miniatures**


via WizKids


A big part of the fun of running games for me is having an excuse to play with toys again. TTRPGs are about the importance of play ([both for kids and adults](https://startplaying.games/blog/posts/tabletop-rpg-mental-health-relationships) ), and having a tactile element can contribute greatly. WizKids makes the official figurines of DnD monsters and heroes. If the GM in your life likes building big battle set pieces, they can always use more minis for their armies. As for what to get, there are[standard blind box sets of DnD monsters](https://startplaying.games/blog/posts/wizkids-underdark-expeditions-review-beholder-mini) or HeroClix that give more quality figures and include Marvel characters if you play[superhero RPGs](https://startplaying.games/blog/posts/best-superhero-ttrpgs-marvel-dc-mcu) .


## **For Players**


### **Third Party DnD Book That Matches Their Vibe**


via Loot Tavern


Many DnD players pick up a Player’s Handbook and that’s it. They don’t want to spend hundreds of dollars building a mini library (or they’d rather spend it on dice). But if you get them something they can actually use in your gams, they’ll eat it up. Thankfully, there’s a lot of great third-party books that do just that. Some add new subclasses, some new magic items, some shift the game’s genre entirely. You can find a good selection at your local game store if you want physical copies to wrap up, but D&D Beyond also offers an ever-increasing list of third-party player content.


Some personal recommendations are[Crooked Moon](https://avantris.com/collections/the-crooked-moon?srsltid=AYCX9vIYU8s4hWg6J-9LBIo3CJAcH_UnuAMFm2syNl_eYLxTudLqu6bY) ,[Ryoko’s Guide to the Yokai Realms](https://loottavern.com/product/ryokos-guide-to-the-yokai-realms-digital/?srsltid=AYCX9vJgRMkkL0FoPua4WuLsh7Asv2Mqa-ukvbIHmqsdIxU5Ra_17T3D) *,*[Humblewood](https://hitpointpress.com/collections/humblewood?tw_source=google&tw_adid=&tw_campaign=23132569907&tw_kwdid=&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23136671899&gbraid=0AAAAACqiQlJIEn_zAd5oInrhWQ3gBYaOs&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIi-HD6IqOmAMVCA9ECB28_AyqEAAYASAAEgJAP_D_BwE) , and **[Kibbles’ Compendium](https://www.kthomebrew.com/shop) .


### **Character Journal**


via Minva


A wonderful gift for the notetaker of the party. A bespoke journal for their current character really gets them immersed in the campaign. Minva has affordable options mostly aimed at DnD, but also makes journals for[Shadowdark](https://startplaying.games/play/shadowdark-rpg) . Searching on Etsy turns up options for[sci-fi TTRPGS](https://startplaying.games/blog/posts/8-sci-fi-ttrpg-recommendations-for-fans-of-star-trek-star-wars-80s-movies-anime-and-more) , such as this[mission log notebook](https://www.etsy.com/listing/4562064108/mission-log-hardcover-journal-retro?ls=a&ga_order=most_relevant&ga_search_type=all&ga_view_type=gallery&ga_search_query=sci+fi+character+journal&ref=sc_gallery-1-2&sr_prefetch=1&pf_from=market&pro=1&frs=1&plkey=EuLaWnnkyyjsuPFQoRRvFSjTFK9a%3ALT731f237bb07111fc966adab7d393d7c348daee68) or this[Star Trek-inspired captain’s log](https://www.etsy.com/listing/4403388637/captains-log-notebook-star-trek-tng?ls=a&ga_order=most_relevant&ga_search_type=all&ga_view_type=gallery&ga_search_query=sci+fi+character+journal&ref=sc_gallery-1-2&sr_prefetch=1&pf_from=market&frs=1&sts=1&plkey=Eu71Mo0AXRJeNnOOazx_7jGkr145%3ALT3cd1d00e52ec98577c6ad847c240168b0d9b032f) .


### **Character Art Commission**


We live firmly in the age of AI– dread it, run from it, ChatGPT-made character “art” comes to my table all the same. We all don’t have expendable income to spend on a drawing of a character that’ll be played for a few months, and the AI gives you your silver Mandalorian Tiefling in seconds.


Since it is gift giving season, though, we have a chance to give work to human artists. Commission them to reserve their time and the giftee can give the details later. You can find plenty of TTRPG artists on Instagram or[Fiverr](https://www.fiverr.com/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc-brand&utm_campaign=G_US_Brand_BrandingDeskTop_Exact&utm_term=one-fiverr_(exact)&utm_content=AdID%5E549600552450%5EKeyword%5Efiverr%5EPlacement%5E%5EDevice%5Ec&caid=731898203&agid=43879774452&ad_id=549600552450&kw=fiverr&lpcat=br_general&show_join=true&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=731898203&gbraid=0AAAAADsPu6sBpRuFHnHFyfs-BZLnGXlKP&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIjPD96JWQmAMVyJHuAR2kQSfzEAAYASAAEgKH5PD_BwE) . I personally work with[this artist](https://www.instagram.com/artivistaa.__/?hl=en) for my campaigns; they have reasonable prices and work in a variety of genres.


### DnD 5.5e Reference Mats


via Total Party Chill


For the DnD player who mostly plays online. These large mats serve as a large mousepad but also as a handy reference for pretty much every rule used in weekly DnD 5.5e play. What you can do on a turn, what each condition means, how resting works, and other useful things are all descirbed with intuitive blurbs and graphics. It's faster than looking up the rules, and can be referenced during other peoples' turn so you know what you can do on yours. The maker,[Total Party Chill](https://totalpartychill.com/collections/play-mats-desk-mats/products/2024-dnd-player-mat-5e-rules-mat) , also has a 5e version for groups that don't want to adopt the new rules!


## **For The Table**


### **Prompt Cards**


via Adams Media


One of the most fun sessions my friend group had in recent memory was a Session Zero. That’s because I brought a deck of cards and let them go wild drawing and answering prompts. It was[The Ultimate RPG Worldbuilding Deck](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1507223870?lv=shuf&channelId=500&plpRedirect=mhFallback&th=1) . In trying to embrace[Daggerheart ’s](https://startplaying.games/play/daggerheart) emphasis on shared worldbuilding, I had each player draw two cards and add something to the world. Each player ended up drawing more than two cards because they got so into it. There are many decks like these out there, and they make great cheap gifts that’ll keep your whole table entertained.


### **A Giant Dice Tray For Important Rolls**


via GameStop


A lot of my players are Dimension 20 fans and so love the Box of Doom concept. Getting my own Box of Doom for in-person games was an easy way to make things more epic. You too can add some dramatic flair to your table with your own Box of Doom. Some 3D print marketplaces[sell a template](https://makerworld.com/en/models/2074282-box-of-doom-dimension-20#profileId-2240671) of the actual thing to make your own. Or you can put your own spin on it by buying a different giant dice tray or decorative roller. GameStop has one[based on classic DnD lore](https://www.gamestop.com/collectibles/statues/products/dungeons-and-dragons-dice-tower-in-faux-bronze-gamestop-exclusive/326035.html) , or you can go with a[more minimalist style](https://www.etsy.com/listing/4328521191/leather-walnut-wood-dice-tray-rpg?gpla=1&gao=1&&utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=shopping_us_ps-a-toys_and_games&utm_custom1=_k_EAIaIQobChMI3aq6spWRmAMVeTRECB3f-R8PEAQYAiABEgIXI_D_BwE_k_&utm_content=go_21791666328_169566861318_716586688965_pla-314535279060_c__4328521191_132930531&utm_custom2=21791666328&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21791666328&gbraid=0AAAAADtcfRLuhsMDttb9Fo_RstFtAZAfH&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI3aq6spWRmAMVeTRECB3f-R8PEAQYAiABEgIXI_D_BwE) .


### **Potion Of Healing Dice**


via sharchetXcreations


I picked[this one](https://www.etsy.com/listing/1448708208/100ml-dd-dice-potion-of-healing-or?gpla=1&gao=1&&utm_medium=cpc&utm_custom2=21500569332&utm_source=google&utm_custom1=_k_EAIaIQobChMIppneje2YmAMVHAVECB06hwenEAQYAiABEgLmefD_BwE_k_&utm_content=go_21500569332_164907277083_707558291651_pla-825885616048_c__1448708208_12768591&utm_campaign=shopping_us_-toys_and_games_e&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21500569332&gbraid=0AAAAADtcfRKOPxYw0frfK9j1C26VyOuuo&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIppneje2YmAMVHAVECB06hwenEAQYAiABEgLmefD_BwE) up from a local shop recently, and it's been a very handy prop. It's bottle made to look like a DnD Potion of Healing that has 2d4 inside. Aside from adding some immersion, it also reminds players what they're supposed to roll when their character drinks a potion. It's been espeically helpful with my casual group at the local game store that's full of newbies. It's a wonderful stocking stuffer for both players and DMs.


### **Local Store Or DriveThruRPG Gift Cards**


via DriveThruRPG


One challenge with many of the ideas on this list is you can’t be sure what people already have. Do your friends actually read the books you give them? Will your GM’s partner get annoyed when they come home with *another* giant piece of DnD terrain?


Keeping this in mind, gift cards are the forever safe option. But we can put a bit more effort in than just Target or Amazon. Your friendly local game store can always use the business, and then it’s in your GM’s hands if they choose to come home with another giant piece of terrain.[DriveThruRPG](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/) is another solid shop, as players and GMs alike can buy new TTRPGs without taking up more shelf space.
